plate.viewWhy: As for the parent: long arms, a tall body and a straight-up shoulder path read best side-on (c1, c2); the census draws it side. The head pushed forward (c3) reads side-on too.
plate.equipment: Smith machine (rails, bar, hooks); bar at mid-thigh height in front of the body (c1); safety pins set (c4); floor line.
plate.start: Standing, feet shoulder-width (c1), arms hanging long with a slight elbow bend, bar at mid-thigh (c1), shoulders relaxed down (c2).
plate.end: Same body; only the shoulders lifted straight up toward the ears, arms still long (c2).

checkpoints.what: Elbows keep only a slight bend, the arms just hang.

checkpoints.label: Straight up
checkpoints.what: Shoulders go up toward the ears and back down, no roll.

checkpoints.label: Head still
checkpoints.what: Head stays level, not pushed forward.

mistake.what: Head pushed forward as the shoulders rise, instead of staying level.
mistake.why: Motra lists "Leaning head forward" first among its common mistakes for this exercise (c3). How often it happens is not measured.
mistake.rankNote: No source measures how often each fault happens. LR-31 step 3: leaning the head forward (c3), first on Motra's common-mistakes list for the Smith shrug. Step 1: no frequency word counts for a fault. Set aside: Motra's "Typical Rep Range" is programming and "Spotting not typically needed due to machine guides" is about spotting; EōS's "At EōS, you’ll commonly find:" is the equipment; Kolber's "the most prevalent regions of injury" (c9) names no fault. Step 2: no quote ties a named fault to harm. Motra's "Stop if neck or shoulder pain occurs" (c4) names no fault; "Avoid hyperextending spine at top" is a Safety Note with no harm word; EōS's "avoid unnecessary strain" is about adjusting the machine (a setup choice); Kolber's "improper attention to exercise technique" (c9) names no fault. Step 3: Motra's list, written for this exercise and the anchor: "Leaning head forward", "Rocking body for momentum" (handlingMistakes[0] until now), "Rounding shoulders", "Excessive elbow bend" (plate.mistake until now), "Dropping weight rapidly". drawable true: the side view shows the head pushed forward of the shoulders, a still sign. Pick changed: plate.mistake moves from the elbow bend to the head; handlingMistakes is reordered with the head first.

tempo.text: Up 2 and down 2 are Motra's 2-1-2 (c11, WEAK), whose Tempo tooltip gives the order eccentric (lowering), bottom pause, concentric (lifting), top pause (R-LB6-2); the page shows three numbers, read as the first three, with no top pause. Its 1 s bottom pause sits between the lowering and the shrug, so it is named here and not written in pause (LR-33). Pause 0: no quote asks for a pause right after the shrug. Motra's "Squeeze trapezius muscles at the top position." gives no pause or seconds. Changed from up 1, down 2 (ACSM or a convention) under R-LB6-2.
